vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pdf-simple-tool
Version: 1.1.0

The skill provides legitimate PDF splitting and PDF-to-Word conversion functionality using standard Node.js libraries (pdf-lib, pdf-parse, and docx). The implementation in node/index.js is straightforward, performing file I/O and document processing exactly as described in SKILL.md, with no evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The code and runtime instructions match the PDF splitting / PDF→Word purpose, but the skill omits an install/runtime spec (Node and npm dependencies) and contains package metadata pointing to an external npm mirror — this mismatch warrants caution before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name, description, SKILL.md, and node/index.js all describe and implement PDF splitting and simple PDF→DOCX conversion — functionality is coherent. However, the skill does not declare that it requires Node or that its npm dependencies must be installed, which is inconsistent with the included code and package.json.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md narrowly instructs the agent to call the two Node functions with absolute file paths and page ranges. The instructions do not ask for unrelated files, environment variables, network endpoints, or broad data collection. Note: the agent (or integrator) must map natural-language requests to absolute filesystem paths — that mapping grants the agent the ability to read arbitrary files the user provides paths for, which is expected for a file-manipulation skill but should be done with care.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec, yet the bundle contains node/index.js plus package.json and a package-lock.json listing dependencies and resolved URLs (to an npm mirror). This is inconsistent: the runtime needs Node and the listed npm packages (pdf-lib, pdf-parse, docx) but the skill does not declare required binaries or provide an install step. The package-lock shows resolved packages from registry.npmmirror.com (a third-party npm mirror) — if an installer were added, that source should be evaluated. Lack of an install mechanism increases the risk of runtime failures or of an operator adding ad-hoc installs without vetting packages.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, which is appropriate for its stated purpose. The only sensitive capability is filesystem access: the implementation reads the inputPath and writes outputPath provided by the caller. That is necessary for file-processing but means the skill will operate on any file paths the agent is directed to use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent/always-on status and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It runs on demand and only performs local file I/O when invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement the PDF split and PDF→Word features it claims, but has an important mismatch: it includes Node code and package metadata but provides no install/runtime instructions. Before installing or enabling it, consider: 1) Only run in a safe environment (sandbox or VM) until dependencies are vetted. 2) Verify the runtime has Node (and compatible version) and install the declared packages from a trusted registry; review package-lock or replace it with one that resolves to an official registry if you rely on automated installs. 3) Confirm you are comfortable with the skill reading the absolute file paths you pass (it will read the input PDF and write the output file). 4) Optionally request the author add an explicit install spec (or declare required binaries) and clarify why the package-lock uses registry.npmmirror.com. If you lack the ability to vet dependencies, do not run this skill on sensitive files or systems.
